reasoning_content:
The circle has center O and diameter AB. The upper half is divided into several sectors. From the figure: starting from ray OB (right side), going counterclockwise: 25° between OB and the first red ray; then 45° between that red ray and the next ray (black line); then the shaded sector between that black ray and the next red ray; then 40° between that red ray and OA (left side).

Wait, let me look at the figure carefully. Angles: 40° is between OA (leftward horizontal) and the red ray going to the upper left. 45° is between the black ray (going upper-right, steep) and the red ray at 25°. 25° is between OB (rightward horizontal) and the red ray at 25°.

So the upper half (180°) is divided as follows: 25° (from OB to the red ray), 45° (from the red ray to the black ray), then the shaded sector (from the black ray to the upper-left red ray), then 40° (from that red ray to OA).

Therefore shaded angle = 180 - 25 - 45 - 40 = 70°.

Probability = 70/360 = 7/36.

Wait, but the shaded sector: between the black ray and the upper-left red ray. Yes, the angles along the upper half: from OB (0°) to 25°: red ray at 25°. From 25° to 25+45=70°: black ray at 70°. From 70° to 70+x: shaded sector ending at the red ray. From that red ray to 180°: 40°, so the red ray is at 140°. Therefore shaded = 140 - 70 = 70°.

Probability = 70/360 = 7/36.

Simplified: 7/36.

Thus the answer: \boxed{7/36}.
content:
Looking at the upper semicircle (180° total), the angles from ray OB to ray OA are: 25°, then 45°, then the shaded sector, then 40°.

Shaded angle = 180° − 25° − 45° − 40° = 70°.

Probability = shaded sector area / total disk area = 70° / 360° = 7/36.

\boxed{7/36}
